# gh-1060: BLOCKED conclusion must park the PR too: status:Blocked is set on the issue but no SM rule reads it — armed PRs loop rework legs forever (live: dart #420)

## Description

## Problem

The rework contract (`### Blocked (agents#827)`: a pass with open threads and no code change is treated as blocked — the leg writes `BLOCKED:` and the ticket moves to `status:Blocked`) updates only the ISSUE's status label. **No SM rule reads `status:Blocked`** — the PR keeps whatever arm it carried (`agent:rework`), and every subsequent tick re-dispatches a rework leg on a ticket the leg itself just declared blocked. Live: dmtools-dart gh-395 / PR #420, 2026-10-18 18:55Z — leg run 39156398849 concluded blocked (issue at `status:Blocked`), PR still armed, next leg would have burned until a human stripped the label manually.

## Root cause

Two parallel "blocked" vocabularies with no bridge: the JS contract writes the issue's `status:Blocked`; the SM's park vocabulary is the PR's `blocked` label (every rule carries `notLabels: [blocked]`). The post-action that moves the ticket to Blocked never touches the PR.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] When a rework/dev leg concludes BLOCKED (the `BLOCKED:` output contract), the post-action ALSO labels the linked PR `blocked` and strips `agent:rework` / `agent:review` arms from both the PR and the issue — one atomic park.
- [ ] Unblocking is symmetric: a human removing `blocked` from the PR (or moving the issue off `status:Blocked`) is enough for the standard lanes to re-admit the pair (no hidden second switch).
- [ ] Unit test: simulated blocked conclusion → PR carries `blocked`, arms gone, next tick dispatches nothing for the pair.

## Non-goals

- Auto-unblocking heuristics (a human owns the blocked state by design).

# gh-1060: BLOCKED conclusion must park the PR too: status:Blocked is set on the issue but no SM rule reads it — armed PRs loop rework legs forever (live: dart #420)

## Description

## Problem

The rework contract (`### Blocked (agents#827)`: a pass with open threads and no code change is treated as blocked — the leg writes `BLOCKED:` and the ticket moves to `status:Blocked`) updates only the ISSUE's status label. **No SM rule reads `status:Blocked`** — the PR keeps whatever arm it carried (`agent:rework`), and every subsequent tick re-dispatches a rework leg on a ticket the leg itself just declared blocked. Live: dmtools-dart gh-395 / PR #420, 2026-10-18 18:55Z — leg run 39156398849 concluded blocked (issue at `status:Blocked`), PR still armed, next leg would have burned until a human stripped the label manually.

## Root cause

Two parallel "blocked" vocabularies with no bridge: the JS contract writes the issue's `status:Blocked`; the SM's park vocabulary is the PR's `blocked` label (every rule carries `notLabels: [blocked]`). The post-action that moves the ticket to Blocked never touches the PR.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] When a rework/dev leg concludes BLOCKED (the `BLOCKED:` output contract), the post-action ALSO labels the linked PR `blocked` and strips `agent:rework` / `agent:review` arms from both the PR and the issue — one atomic park.
- [ ] Unblocking is symmetric: a human removing `blocked` from the PR (or moving the issue off `status:Blocked`) is enough for the standard lanes to re-admit the pair (no hidden second switch).
- [ ] Unit test: simulated blocked conclusion → PR carries `blocked`, arms gone, next tick dispatches nothing for the pair.

## Non-goals

- Auto-unblocking heuristics (a human owns the blocked state by design).

# gh-1060: BLOCKED conclusion must park the PR too: status:Blocked is set on the issue but no SM rule reads it — armed PRs loop rework legs forever (live: dart #420)

## Description

## Problem

The rework contract (`### Blocked (agents#827)`: a pass with open threads and no code change is treated as blocked — the leg writes `BLOCKED:` and the ticket moves to `status:Blocked`) updates only the ISSUE's status label. **No SM rule reads `status:Blocked`** — the PR keeps whatever arm it carried (`agent:rework`), and every subsequent tick re-dispatches a rework leg on a ticket the leg itself just declared blocked. Live: dmtools-dart gh-395 / PR #420, 2026-10-18 18:55Z — leg run 39156398849 concluded blocked (issue at `status:Blocked`), PR still armed, next leg would have burned until a human stripped the label manually.

## Root cause

Two parallel "blocked" vocabularies with no bridge: the JS contract writes the issue's `status:Blocked`; the SM's park vocabulary is the PR's `blocked` label (every rule carries `notLabels: [blocked]`). The post-action that moves the ticket to Blocked never touches the PR.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] When a rework/dev leg concludes BLOCKED (the `BLOCKED:` output contract), the post-action ALSO labels the linked PR `blocked` and strips `agent:rework` / `agent:review` arms from both the PR and the issue — one atomic park.
- [ ] Unblocking is symmetric: a human removing `blocked` from the PR (or moving the issue off `status:Blocked`) is enough for the standard lanes to re-admit the pair (no hidden second switch).
- [ ] Unit test: simulated blocked conclusion → PR carries `blocked`, arms gone, next tick dispatches nothing for the pair.

## Non-goals

- Auto-unblocking heuristics (a human owns the blocked state by design).

blocks.text:
# gh-1060: BLOCKED conclusion must park the PR too: status:Blocked is set on the issue but no SM rule reads it — armed PRs loop rework legs forever (live: dart #420)

## Description

## Problem

The rework contract (`### Blocked (agents#827)`: a pass with open threads and no code change is treated as blocked — the leg writes `BLOCKED:` and the ticket moves to `status:Blocked`) updates only the ISSUE's status label. **No SM rule reads `status:Blocked`** — the PR keeps whatever arm it carried (`agent:rework`), and every subsequent tick re-dispatches a rework leg on a ticket the leg itself just declared blocked. Live: dmtools-dart gh-395 / PR #420, 2026-10-18 18:55Z — leg run 39156398849 concluded blocked (issue at `status:Blocked`), PR still armed, next leg would have burned until a human stripped the label manually.

## Root cause

Two parallel "blocked" vocabularies with no bridge: the JS contract writes the issue's `status:Blocked`; the SM's park vocabulary is the PR's `blocked` label (every rule carries `notLabels: [blocked]`). The post-action that moves the ticket to Blocked never touches the PR.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] When a rework/dev leg concludes BLOCKED (the `BLOCKED:` output contract), the post-action ALSO labels the linked PR `blocked` and strips `agent:rework` / `agent:review` arms from both the PR and the issue — one atomic park.
- [ ] Unblocking is symmetric: a human removing `blocked` from the PR (or moving the issue off `status:Blocked`) is enough for the standard lanes to re-admit the pair (no hidden second switch).
- [ ] Unit test: simulated blocked conclusion → PR carries `blocked`, arms gone, next tick dispatches nothing for the pair.

## Non-goals

- Auto-unblocking heuristics (a human owns the blocked state by design).

# gh-1060: BLOCKED conclusion must park the PR too: status:Blocked is set on the issue but no SM rule reads it — armed PRs loop rework legs forever (live: dart #420)

## Description

## Problem

The rework contract (`### Blocked (agents#827)`: a pass with open threads and no code change is treated as blocked — the leg writes `BLOCKED:` and the ticket moves to `status:Blocked`) updates only the ISSUE's status label. **No SM rule reads `status:Blocked`** — the PR keeps whatever arm it carried (`agent:rework`), and every subsequent tick re-dispatches a rework leg on a ticket the leg itself just declared blocked. ## Root cause

Two parallel "blocked" vocabularies with no bridge: the JS contract writes the issue's `status:Blocked`; the SM's park vocabulary is the PR's `blocked` label (every rule carries `notLabels: [blocked]`). The post-action that moves the ticket to Blocked never touches the PR.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] When a rework/dev leg concludes BLOCKED (the `BLOCKED:` output contract), the post-action ALSO labels the linked PR `blocked` and strips `agent:rework` / `agent:review` arms from both the PR and the issue — one atomic park.

- [ ] Unit test: simulated blocked conclusion → PR carries `blocked`, arms gone, next tick dispatches nothing for the pair.

## Non-goals

- Auto-unblocking heuristics (a human owns the blocked state by design).

# gh-1060: BLOCKED conclusion must park the PR too: status:Blocked is set on the issue but no SM rule reads it — armed PRs loop rework legs forever (live: dart #420)

## Description

## Problem

The rework contract (`### Blocked (agents#827)`: a pass with open threads and no code change is treated as blocked — the leg writes `BLOCKED:` and the ticket moves to `status:Blocked`) updates only the ISSUE's status label. **No SM rule reads `status:Blocked`** — the PR keeps whatever arm it carried (`agent:rework`), and every subsequent tick re-dispatches a rework leg on a ticket the leg itself just declared blocked. Live: dmtools-dart gh-395 / PR #420, 2026-10-18 18:55Z — leg run 39156398849 concluded blocked (issue at `status:Blocked`), PR still armed, next leg would have burned until a human stripped the label manually.

## Root cause

Two parallel "blocked" vocabularies with no bridge: the JS contract writes the issue's `status:Blocked`; the SM's park vocabulary is the PR's `blocked` label (every rule carries `notLabels: [blocked]`). The post-action that moves the ticket to Blocked never touches the PR.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] When a rework/dev leg concludes BLOCKED (the `BLOCKED:` output contract), the post-action ALSO labels the linked PR `blocked` and strips `agent:rework` / `agent:review` arms from both the PR and the issue — one atomic park.
- [ ] Unblocking is symmetric: a human removing `blocked` from the PR (or moving the issue off `status:Blocked`) is enough for the standard lanes to re-admit the pair (no hidden second switch).
- [ ] Unit test: simulated blocked conclusion → PR carries `blocked`, arms gone, next tick dispatches nothing for the pair.

## Non-goals

- Auto-unblocking heuristics (a human owns the blocked state by design).

# gh-1060: BLOCKED conclusion must park the PR too: status:Blocked is set on the issue but no SM rule reads it — armed PRs loop rework legs forever (live: dart #420)

## Description

## Problem

The rework contract (`### Blocked (agents#827)`: a pass with open threads and no code change is treated as blocked — the leg writes `BLOCKED:` and the ticket moves to `status:Blocked`) updates only the ISSUE's status label. **No SM rule reads `status:Blocked`** — the PR keeps whatever arm it carried (`agent:rework`), and every subsequent tick re-dispatches a rework leg on a ticket the leg itself just declared blocked. Live: dmtools-dart gh-395 / PR #420, 2026-10-18 18:55Z — leg run 39156398849 concluded blocked (issue at `status:Blocked`), PR still armed, next leg would have burned until a human stripped the label manually.

## Root cause

Two parallel "blocked" vocabularies with no bridge: the JS contract writes the issue's `status:Blocked`; the SM's park vocabulary is the PR's `blocked` label (every rule carries `notLabels: [blocked]`). The post-action that moves the ticket to Blocked never touches the PR.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] When a rework/dev leg concludes BLOCKED (the `BLOCKED:` output contract), the post-action ALSO labels the linked PR `blocked` and strips `agent:rework` / `agent:review` arms from both the PR and the issue — one atomic park.
- [ ] Unblocking is symmetric: a human removing `blocked` from the PR (or moving the issue off `status:Blocked`) is enough for the standard lanes to re-admit the pair (no hidden second switch).
- [ ] Unit test: simulated blocked conclusion → PR carries `blocked`, arms gone, next tick dispatches nothing for the pair.

## Non-goals

- Auto-unblocking heuristics (a human owns the blocked state by design).

# gh-1060: BLOCKED conclusion must park the PR too: status:Blocked is set on the issue but no SM rule reads it — armed PRs loop rework legs forever (live: dart #420)

## Description

## Problem

The rework contract (`### Blocked (agents#827)`: a pass with open threads and no code change is treated as blocked — the leg writes `BLOCKED:` and the ticket moves to `status:Blocked`) updates only the ISSUE's status label. **No SM rule reads `status:Blocked`** — the PR keeps whatever arm it carried (`agent:rework`), and every subsequent tick re-dispatches a rework leg on a ticket the leg itself just declared blocked. Live: dmtools-dart gh-395 / PR #420, 2026-10-18 18:55Z — leg run 39156398849 concluded blocked (issue at `status:Blocked`), PR still armed, next leg would have burned until a human stripped the label manually.

## Root cause

Two parallel "blocked" vocabularies with no bridge: the JS contract writes the issue's `status:Blocked`; the SM's park vocabulary is the PR's `blocked` label (every rule carries `notLabels: [blocked]`). The post-action that moves the ticket to Blocked never touches the PR.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] When a rework/dev leg concludes BLOCKED (the `BLOCKED:` output contract), the post-action ALSO labels the linked PR `blocked` and strips `agent:rework` / `agent:review` arms from both the PR and the issue — one atomic park.
- [ ] Unblocking is symmetric: a human removing `blocked` from the PR (or moving the issue off `status:Blocked`) is enough for the standard lanes to re-admit the pair (no hidden second switch).
- [ ] Unit test: simulated blocked conclusion → PR carries `blocked`, arms gone, next tick dispatches nothing for the pair.

## Non-goals

- Auto-unblocking heuristics (a human owns the blocked state by design).

blocks.text:
# gh-1060: BLOCKED conclusion must park the PR too: status:Blocked is set on the issue but no SM rule reads it — armed PRs loop rework legs forever (live: dart #420)

## Description

## Problem

The rework contract (`### Blocked (agents#827)`: a pass with open threads and no code change is treated as blocked — the leg writes `BLOCKED:` and the ticket moves to `status:Blocked`) updates only the ISSUE's status label. **No SM rule reads `status:Blocked`** — the PR keeps whatever arm it carried (`agent:rework`), and every subsequent tick re-dispatches a rework leg on a ticket the leg itself just declared blocked. Live: dmtools-dart gh-395 / PR #420, 2026-10-18 18:55Z — leg run 39156398849 concluded blocked (issue at `status:Blocked`), PR still armed, next leg would have burned until a human stripped the label manually.

## Root cause

Two parallel "blocked" vocabularies with no bridge: the JS contract writes the issue's `status:Blocked`; the SM's park vocabulary is the PR's `blocked` label (every rule carries `notLabels: [blocked]`). The post-action that moves the ticket to Blocked never touches the PR.

## Acceptance criteria

# gh-1060: BLOCKED conclusion must park the PR too: status:Blocked is set on the issue but no SM rule reads it — armed PRs loop rework legs forever (live: dart #420)

## Description

## Problem

The rework contract (`### Blocked (agents#827)`: a pass with open threads and no code change is treated as blocked — the leg writes `BLOCKED:` and the ticket moves to `status:Blocked`) updates only the ISSUE's status label. **No SM rule reads `status:Blocked`** — the PR keeps whatever arm it carried (`agent:rework`), and every subsequent tick re-dispatches a rework leg on a ticket the leg itself just declared blocked. Live: dmtools-dart gh-395 / PR #420, 2026-10-18 18:55Z — leg run 39156398849 concluded blocked (issue at `status:Blocked`), PR still armed, next leg would have burned until a human stripped the label manually.

## Root cause

Two parallel "blocked" vocabularies with no bridge: the JS contract writes the issue's `status:Blocked`; the SM's park vocabulary is the PR's `blocked` label (every rule carries `notLabels: [blocked]`). The post-action that moves the ticket to Blocked never touches the PR.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] When a rework/dev leg concludes BLOCKED (the `BLOCKED:` output contract), the post-action ALSO labels the linked PR `blocked` and strips `agent:rework` / `agent:review` arms from both the PR and the issue — one atomic park.
- [ ] Unblocking is symmetric: a human removing `blocked` from the PR (or moving the issue off `status:Blocked`) is enough for the standard lanes to re-admit the pair (no hidden second switch).
- [ ] Unit test: simulated blocked conclusion → PR carries `blocked`, arms gone, next tick dispatches nothing for the pair.

## Non-goals

- Auto-unblocking heuristics (a human owns the blocked state by design).

# gh-1060: BLOCKED conclusion must park the PR too: status:Blocked is set on the issue but no SM rule reads it — armed PRs loop rework legs forever (live: dart #420)

## Description

## Problem

The rework contract (`### Blocked (agents#827)`: a pass with open threads and no code change is treated as blocked — the leg writes `BLOCKED:` and the ticket moves to `status:Blocked`) updates only the ISSUE's status label. **No SM rule reads `status:Blocked`** — the PR keeps whatever arm it carried (`agent:rework`), and every subsequent tick re-dispatches a rework leg on a ticket the leg itself just declared blocked. Live: dmtools-dart gh-395 / PR #420, 2026-10-18 18:55Z — leg run 39156398849 concluded blocked (issue at `status:Blocked`), PR still armed, next leg would have burned until a human stripped the label manually.

## Root cause

Two parallel "blocked" vocabularies with no bridge: the JS contract writes the issue's `status:Blocked`; the SM's park vocabulary is the PR's `blocked` label (every rule carries `notLabels: [blocked]`). The post-action that moves the ticket to Blocked never touches the PR.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] When a rework/dev leg concludes BLOCKED (the `BLOCKED:` output contract), the post-action ALSO labels the linked PR `blocked` and strips `agent:rework` / `agent:review` arms from both the PR and the issue — one atomic park.
- [ ] Unblocking is symmetric: a human removing `blocked` from the PR (or moving the issue off `status:Blocked`) is enough for the standard lanes to re-admit the pair (no hidden second switch).
- [ ] Unit test: simulated blocked conclusion → PR carries `blocked`, arms gone, next tick dispatches nothing for the pair.

## Non-goals

- Auto-unblocking heuristics (a human owns the blocked state by design).

Acceptance criteria:
1. When a rework/dev leg concludes BLOCKED, the post-action ALSO labels the linked PR `blocked` and strips `agent:rework`/`agent:review` arms from both the PR and the issue — one atomic park.
2. Unblocking symmetric: human removing `blocked` from the PR (or moving issue off status:Blocked) re-admits the pair. — Since PR `blocked` label already freezes the issue-carier items in `_prSideBlockedLabel` and PR-side `notLabels: [blocked]` in rules, removing the label re-admits. Need to verify issue rules also carry `blocked` in notLabels... In gh mode, issue rules match on issue labels; do they carry notLabels blocked? Let's check what labels freeze issue rules. `_issueCarrierGuardsFail` — check that function. Also, does `status:Blocked` on the issue freeze issue rules? The ticket says "No SM rule reads status:Blocked". AC2 says moving issue off status:Blocked is enough for standard lanes to re-admit the pair — that means issue rules should exclude `status:Blocked` issues too? Actually re-read: "Unblocking is symmetric: a human removing `blocked` from the PR (or moving the issue off `status:Blocked`) is enough for the standard lanes to re-admit the pair (no hidden second switch)." Hmm — so both directions must re-admit: remove PR blocked label OR remove issue status:Blocked label. If SM rules only freeze on the PR `blocked` label, then removing `blocked` from PR re-admits, but if the issue still has `status:Blocked`... would rules re-admit? For issue-carier rules: they query issues and match labels. Does the issue still carry `agent:rework`? We strip it. Does `status:Blocked` freeze issue rules? Apparently not — "No SM rule reads status:Blocked". # gh-1060: BLOCKED conclusion must park the PR too: status:Blocked is set on the issue but no SM rule reads it — armed PRs loop rework legs forever (live: dart #420)

## Description

## Problem

The rework contract (`### Blocked (agents#827)`: a pass with open threads and no code change is treated as blocked — the leg writes `BLOCKED:` and the ticket moves to `status:Blocked`) updates only the ISSUE's status label. **No SM rule reads `status:Blocked`** — the PR keeps whatever arm it carried (`agent:rework`), and every subsequent tick re-dispatches a rework leg on a ticket the leg itself just declared blocked. Live: dmtools-dart gh-395 / PR #420, 2026-10-18 18:55Z — leg run 39156398849 concluded blocked (issue at `status:Blocked`), PR still armed, next leg would have burned until a human stripped the label manually.

## Root cause

Two parallel "blocked" vocabularies with no bridge: the JS contract writes the issue's `status:Blocked`; the SM's park vocabulary is the PR's `blocked` label (every rule carries `notLabels: [blocked]`). The post-action that moves the ticket to Blocked never touches the PR.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] When a rework/dev leg concludes BLOCKED (the `BLOCKED:` output contract), the post-action ALSO labels the linked PR `blocked` and strips `agent:rework` / `agent:review` arms from both the PR and the issue — one atomic park.
- [ ] Unblocking is symmetric: a human removing `blocked` from the PR (or moving the issue off `status:Blocked`) is enough for the standard lanes to re-admit the pair (no hidden second switch).
- [ ] Unit test: simulated blocked conclusion → PR carries `blocked`, arms gone, next tick dispatches nothing for the pair.

## Non-goals

- Auto-unblocking heuristics (a human owns the blocked state by design).

# gh-1060: BLOCKED conclusion must park the PR too: status:Blocked is set on the issue but no SM rule reads it — armed PRs loop rework legs forever (live: dart #420)

## Description

## Problem

The rework contract (`### Blocked (agents#827)`: a pass with open threads and no code change is treated as blocked — the leg writes `BLOCKED:` and the ticket moves to `status:Blocked`) updates only the ISSUE's status label. **No SM rule reads `status:Blocked`** — the PR keeps whatever arm it carried (`agent:rework`), and every subsequent tick re-dispatches a rework leg on a ticket the leg itself just declared blocked. Live: dmtools-dart gh-395 / PR #420, 2026-10-18 18:55Z — leg run 39156398849 concluded blocked (issue at `status:Blocked`), PR still armed, next leg would have burned until a human stripped the label manually.

## Root cause

Two parallel "blocked" vocabularies with no bridge: the JS contract writes the issue's `status:Blocked`; the SM's park vocabulary is the PR's `blocked` label (every rule carries `notLabels: [blocked]`). The post-action that moves the ticket to Blocked never touches the PR.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] When a rework/dev leg concludes BLOCKED (the `BLOCKED:` output contract), the post-action ALSO labels the linked PR `blocked` and strips `agent:rework` / `agent:review` arms from both the PR and the issue — one atomic park.
- [ ] Unblocking is symmetric: a human removing `blocked` from the PR (or moving the issue off `status:Blocked`) is enough for the standard lanes to re-admit the pair (no hidden second switch).
- [ ] Unit test: simulated blocked conclusion → PR carries `blocked`, arms gone, next tick dispatches nothing for the pair.

## Non-goals

- Auto-unblocking heuristics (a human owns the blocked state by design).

# gh-1060: BLOCKED conclusion must park the PR too: status:Blocked is set on the issue but no SM rule reads it — armed PRs loop rework legs forever (live: dart #420)

## Description

## Problem

The rework contract (`### Blocked (agents#827)`: a pass with open threads and no code change is treated as blocked — the leg writes `BLOCKED:` and the ticket moves to `status:Blocked`) updates only the ISSUE's status label. **No SM rule reads `status:Blocked`** — the PR keeps whatever arm it carried (`agent:rework`), and every subsequent tick re-dispatches a rework leg on a ticket the leg itself just declared blocked. Live: dmtools-dart gh-395 / PR #420, 2026-10-18 18:55Z — leg run 39156398849 concluded blocked (issue at `status:Blocked`), PR still armed, next leg would have burned until a human stripped the label manually.

## Root cause

Two parallel "blocked" vocabularies with no bridge: the JS contract writes the issue's `status:Blocked`; the SM's park vocabulary is the PR's `blocked` label (every rule carries `notLabels: [blocked]`). The post-action that moves the ticket to Blocked never touches the PR.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] When a rework/dev leg concludes BLOCKED (the `BLOCKED:` output contract), the post-action ALSO labels the linked PR `blocked` and strips `agent:rework` / `agent:review` arms from both the PR and the issue — one atomic park.
- [ ] Unblocking is symmetric: a human removing `blocked` from the PR (or moving the issue off `status:Blocked`) is enough for the standard lanes to re-admit the pair (no hidden second switch).
- [ ] Unit test: simulated blocked conclusion → PR carries `blocked`, arms gone, next tick dispatches nothing for the pair.

## Non-goals

- Auto-unblocking heuristics (a human owns the blocked state by design).

1. When a rework/dev leg concludes BLOCKED, the post-action ALSO labels the linked PR `blocked` and strips `agent:rework`/`agent:review` arms from both the PR and the issue — one atomic park.
2. Unblocking symmetric: human removing `blocked` from the PR (or moving issue off status:Blocked) re-admits the pair. — Since PR `blocked` label already freezes the issue-carier items in `_prSideBlockedLabel` and PR-side `notLabels: [blocked]` in rules, removing the label re-admits. Need to verify issue rules also carry `blocked` in notLabels... In gh mode, issue rules match on issue labels; do they carry notLabels blocked? Let's check what labels freeze issue rules. `_issueCarrierGuardsFail` — check that function. Also, does `status:Blocked` on the issue freeze issue rules? The ticket says "No SM rule reads status:Blocked". AC2 says moving issue off status:Blocked is enough for standard lanes to re-admit the pair — that means issue rules should exclude `status:Blocked` issues too? Actually re-read: "Unblocking is symmetric: a human removing `blocked` from the PR (or moving the issue off `status:Blocked`) is enough for the standard lanes to re-admit the pair (no hidden second switch)." Hmm — so both directions must re-admit: remove PR blocked label OR remove issue status:Blocked label. If SM rules only freeze on the PR `blocked` label, then removing `blocked` from PR re-admits, but if the issue still has `status:Blocked`... would rules re-admit? For issue-carier rules: they query issues and match labels. Does the issue still carry `agent:rework`? We strip it. Does `status:Blocked` freeze issue rules? Apparently not — "No SM rule reads status:Blocked". So an issue with `status:Blocked` but no arms and no PR blocked label — would dev-on-assignment re-derive? gh-944 rule: matches assigned issues with no loop marker labels — yes it would re-dispatch. Hmm, but that's arguably the desired re-admission per AC2: "moving the issue off status:Blocked is enough for re-admission" — means while status:Blocked remains, should it stay frozen? AC2's parenthetical says removing EITHER is enough. That implies while status:Blocked is present but PR blocked was removed... ambiguous. Simplest reading: no hidden second switch — a single action suffices to unblock. The two "blocked" indicators should be equivalent. So ideally: PR blocked label OR issue status:Blocked label both freeze; removing either... if both are set, removing one leaves the other — "enough" implies removing one suffices even if the other remains? That would require SM to treat them as one logical state OR the post-action to set both and... hmm.

Actually the cleanest interpretation given the SM engine: the PR `blocked` label is the park vocabulary that every rule reads (`notLabels: [blocked]` on PR rules, `_prSideBlockedLabel` for issue-carier rules). The fix: post-action sets PR `blocked` + strips arms on both carriers. AC2 first half satisfied. Second half: "moving the issue off status:Blocked" — for that to re-admit, `status:Blocked` must also freeze; but it currently doesn't freeze anything, so moving off it is trivialy "enough" (it never blocked re-admission in the SM). Wait but does the issue-carier freeze apply through the PR? `_prLabelGuardsFail` reads the linked PR's labels for issue-carier rules. So once PR gets `blocked`, issue rules freeze too. Removing PR `blocked` unfreezes. And `status:Blocked` on issue is never read by SM — so it neither blocks nor requires clearing. "Moving the issue off status:Blocked is enough for re-admission" holds trivialy. # gh-1060: BLOCKED conclusion must park the PR too: status:Blocked is set on the issue but no SM rule reads it — armed PRs loop rework legs forever (live: dart #420)

## Description

## Problem

The rework contract (`### Blocked (agents#827)`: a pass with open threads and no code change is treated as blocked — the leg writes `BLOCKED:` and the ticket moves to `status:Blocked`) updates only the ISSUE's status label. **No SM rule reads `status:Blocked`** — the PR keeps whatever arm it carried (`agent:rework`), and every subsequent tick re-dispatches a rework leg on a ticket the leg itself just declared blocked. Live: dmtools-dart gh-395 / PR #420, 2026-10-18 18:55Z — leg run 39156398849 concluded blocked (issue at `status:Blocked`), PR still armed, next leg would have burned until a human stripped the label manually.

## Root cause

Two parallel "blocked" vocabularies with no bridge: the JS contract writes the issue's `status:Blocked`; the SM's park vocabulary is the PR's `blocked` label (every rule carries `notLabels: [blocked]`). The post-action that moves the ticket to Blocked never touches the PR.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] When a rework/dev leg concludes BLOCKED (the `BLOCKED:` output contract), the post-action ALSO labels the linked PR `blocked` and strips `agent:rework` / `agent:review` arms from both the PR and the issue — one atomic park.
- [ ] Unblocking is symmetric: a human removing `blocked` from the PR (or moving the issue off `status:Blocked`) is enough for the standard lanes to re-admit the pair (no hidden second switch).
- [ ] Unit test: simulated blocked conclusion → PR carries `blocked`, arms gone, next tick dispatches nothing for the pair.

## Non-goals

- Auto-unblocking heuristics (a human owns the blocked state by design).

# gh-1060: BLOCKED conclusion must park the PR too: status:Blocked is set on the issue but no SM rule reads it — armed PRs loop rework legs forever (live: dart #420)

## Description

## Problem

The rework contract (`### Blocked (agents#827)`: a pass with open threads and no code change is treated as blocked — the leg writes `BLOCKED:` and the ticket moves to `status:Blocked`) updates only the ISSUE's status label. **No SM rule reads `status:Blocked`** — the PR keeps whatever arm it carried (`agent:rework`), and every subsequent tick re-dispatches a rework leg on a ticket the leg itself just declared blocked. Live: dmtools-dart gh-395 / PR #420, 2026-10-18 18:55Z — leg run 39156398849 concluded blocked (issue at `status:Blocked`), PR still armed, next leg would have burned until a human stripped the label manually.

## Root cause

Two parallel "blocked" vocabularies with no bridge: the JS contract writes the issue's `status:Blocked`; the SM's park vocabulary is the PR's `blocked` label (every rule carries `notLabels: [blocked]`). The post-action that moves the ticket to Blocked never touches the PR.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] When a rework/dev leg concludes BLOCKED (the `BLOCKED:` output contract), the post-action ALSO labels the linked PR `blocked` and strips `agent:rework` / `agent:review` arms from both the PR and the issue — one atomic park.
- [ ] Unblocking is symmetric: a human removing `blocked` from the PR (or moving the issue off `status:Blocked`) is enough for the standard lanes to re-admit the pair (no hidden second switch).
- [ ] Unit test: simulated blocked conclusion → PR carries `blocked`, arms gone, next tick dispatches nothing for the pair.

## Non-goals

- Auto-unblocking heuristics (a human owns the blocked state by design).

Acceptance criteria:
1. When a rework/dev leg concludes BLOCKED, the post-action ALSO labels the linked PR `blocked` and strips `agent:rework`/`agent:review` arms from both the PR and the issue — one atomic park.
2. Unblocking symmetric: human removing `blocked` from the PR (or moving issue off status:Blocked) re-admits the pair. — Since PR `blocked` label already freezes the issue-carier items in `_prSideBlockedLabel` and PR-side `notLabels: [blocked]` in rules, removing the label re-admits. Need to verify issue rules also carry `blocked` in notLabels... In gh mode, issue rules match on issue labels; do they carry notLabels blocked? Let's check what labels freeze issue rules. `_issueCarrierGuardsFail` — check that function. Also, does `status:Blocked` on the issue freeze issue rules? The ticket says "No SM rule reads status:Blocked". AC2 says moving issue off status:Blocked is enough for standard lanes to re-admit the pair — that means issue rules should exclude `status:Blocked` issues too? Actually re-read: "Unblocking is symmetric: a human removing `blocked` from the PR (or moving the issue off `status:Blocked`) is enough for the standard lanes to re-admit the pair (no hidden second switch)." Hmm — so both directions must re-admit: remove PR blocked label OR remove issue status:Blocked label. If SM rules only freeze on the PR `blocked` label, then removing `blocked` from PR re-admits, but if the issue still has `status:Blocked`... would rules re-admit? For issue-carier rules: they query issues and match labels. Does the issue still carry `agent:rework`? We strip it. Does `status:Blocked` freeze issue rules? Apparently not — "No SM rule reads status:Blocked". So an issue with `status:Blocked` but no arms and no PR blocked label — would dev-on-assignment re-derive? gh-944 rule: matches assigned issues with no loop marker labels — yes it would re-dispatch. Hmm, but that's arguably the desired re-admission per AC2: "moving the issue off status:Blocked is enough for re-admission" — means while status:Blocked remains, should it stay frozen? AC2's parenthetical says removing EITHER is enough. That implies while status:Blocked is present but PR blocked was removed... ambiguous. Simplest reading: no hidden second switch — a single action suffices to unblock. The two "blocked" indicators should be equivalent. So ideally: PR blocked label OR issue status:Blocked label both freeze; removing either... if both are set, removing one leaves the other — "enough" implies removing one suffices even if the other remains? That would require SM to treat them as one logical state OR the post-action to set both and... hmm.

Actually the cleanest interpretation given the SM engine: the PR `blocked` label is the park vocabulary that every rule reads (`notLabels: [blocked]` on PR rules, `_prSideBlockedLabel` for issue-carier rules). The fix: post-action sets PR `blocked` + strips arms on both carriers. AC2 first half satisfied. Second half: "moving the issue off status:Blocked" — for that to re-admit, `status:Blocked` must also freeze; but it currently doesn't freeze anything, so moving off it is trivialy "enough" (it never blocked re-admission in the SM). Wait but does the issue-carier freeze apply through the PR? `_prLabelGuardsFail` reads the linked PR's labels for issue-carier rules. So once PR gets `blocked`, issue rules freeze too. If a human removes PR blocked but leaves issue status:Blocked, pair re-admits — and that's per AC2 acceptable ("a human owns the blocked state by design", non-goal auto-unblock). Actually strictly, AC2 says both are sufficient paths; it doesn't say the states must be synced. But for robustness, maybe also strip status:Blocked when PR blocked removed? # gh-1060: BLOCKED conclusion must park the PR too: status:Blocked is set on the issue but no SM rule reads it — armed PRs loop rework legs forever (live: dart #420)

## Description

## Problem

The rework contract (`### Blocked (agents#827)`: a pass with open threads and no code change is treated as blocked — the leg writes `BLOCKED:` and the ticket moves to `status:Blocked`) updates only the ISSUE's status label. **No SM rule reads `status:Blocked`** — the PR keeps whatever arm it carried (`agent:rework`), and every subsequent tick re-dispatches a rework leg on a ticket the leg itself just declared blocked. Live: dmtools-dart gh-395 / PR #420, 2026-10-18 18:55Z — leg run 39156398849 concluded blocked (issue at `status:Blocked`), PR still armed, next leg would have burned until a human stripped the label manually.

## Root cause

Two parallel "blocked" vocabularies with no bridge: the JS contract writes the issue's `status:Blocked`; the SM's park vocabulary is the PR's `blocked` label (every rule carries `notLabels: [blocked]`). The post-action that moves the ticket to Blocked never touches the PR.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] When a rework/dev leg concludes BLOCKED (the `BLOCKED:` output contract), the post-action ALSO labels the linked PR `blocked` and strips `agent:rework` / `agent:review` arms from both the PR and the issue — one atomic park.
- [ ] Unblocking is symmetric: a human removing `blocked` from the PR (or moving the issue off `status:Blocked`) is enough for the standard lanes to re-admit the pair (no hidden second switch).
- [ ] Unit test: simulated blocked conclusion → PR carries `blocked`, arms gone, next tick dispatches nothing for the pair.

## Non-goals

- Auto-unblocking heuristics (a human owns the blocked state by design).

Unblocking symmetric: human removing `blocked` from the PR (or moving issue off status:Blocked) re-admits the pair. — Since PR `blocked` label already freezes the issue-carier items in `_prSideBlockedLabel` and PR-side `notLabels: [blocked]` in rules, removing the label re-admits. Actually re-read: "Unblocking is symmetric: a human removing `blocked` from the PR (or moving the issue off `status:Blocked`) is enough for the standard lanes to re-admit the pair (no hidden second switch)." Hmm — so both directions must re-admit: remove PR blocked label OR remove issue status:Blocked label. If SM rules only freeze on the PR `blocked` label, then removing `blocked` from PR re-admits, but if the issue still has `status:Blocked`... would rules re-admit? For issue-carier rules: they query issues and match labels. Does the issue still carry `agent:rework`? We strip it. Does `status:Blocked` freeze issue rules? Apparently not — "No SM rule reads status:Blocked". So an issue with `status:Blocked` but no arms and no PR blocked label — would dev-on-assignment re-derive? gh-944 rule: matches assigned issues with no loop marker labels — yes it would re-dispatch. Hmm, but that's arguably the desired re-admission per AC2: "moving the issue off status:Blocked is enough for re-admission" — means while status:Blocked remains, should it stay frozen? AC2's parenthetical says removing EITHER is enough. That implies while status:Blocked is present but PR blocked was removed... ambiguous. So ideally: PR blocked label OR issue status:Blocked label both freeze; removing either... if both are set, removing one leaves the other — "enough" implies removing one suffices even if the other remains? Actually the cleanest interpretation given the SM engine: the PR `blocked` label is the park vocabulary that every rule reads (`notLabels: [blocked]` on PR rules, `_prSideBlockedLabel` for issue-carier rules). Acceptance criteria:
1. When a rework/dev leg concludes BLOCKED, the post-action ALSO labels the linked PR `blocked` and strips `agent:rework`/`agent:review` arms from both the PR and the issue — one atomic park.
2. Unblocking symmetric: human removing `blocked` from the PR (or moving issue off status:Blocked) re-admits the pair. — Since PR `blocked` label already freezes the issue-carier items in `_prSideBlockedLabel` and PR-side `notLabels: [blocked]` in rules, removing the label re-admits. Need to verify issue rules also carry `blocked` in notLabels... In gh mode, issue rules match on issue labels; do they carry notLabels blocked? Let's check what labels freeze issue rules. `_issueCarrierGuardsFail` — check that function. Also, does `status:Blocked` on the issue freeze issue rules? The ticket says "No SM rule reads status:Blocked". AC2 says moving issue off status:Blocked is enough for standard lanes to re-admit the pair — that means issue rules should exclude `status:Blocked` issues too? Actually re-read: "Unblocking is symmetric: a human removing `blocked` from the PR (or moving the issue off `status:Blocked`) is enough for the standard lanes to re-admit the pair (no hidden second switch)." Hmm — so both directions must re-admit: remove PR blocked label OR remove issue status:Blocked label. If SM rules only freeze on the PR `blocked` label, then removing `blocked` from PR re-admits, but if the issue still has `status:Blocked`... would rules re-admit? For issue-carier rules: they query issues and match labels. Does the issue still carry `agent:rework`? We strip it. Does `status:Blocked` freeze issue rules? Apparently not — "No SM rule reads status:Blocked". So an issue with `status:Blocked` but no arms and no PR blocked label — would dev-on-assignment re-derive? gh-944 rule: matches assigned issues with no loop marker labels — yes it would re-dispatch. Hmm, but that's arguably the desired re-admission per AC2: "moving the issue off status:Blocked is enough for re-admission" — means while status:Blocked remains, should it stay frozen? AC2's parenthetical says removing EITHER is enough. That implies while status:Blocked is present but PR blocked was removed... ambiguous. Simplest reading: no hidden second switch — a single action suffices to unblock. The two "blocked" indicators should be equivalent. So ideally: PR blocked label OR issue status:Blocked label both freeze; removing either... if both are set, removing one leaves the other — "enough" implies removing one suffices even if the other remains? That would require SM to treat them as one logical state OR the post-action to set both and... hmm.

Actually the cleanest interpretation given the SM engine: the PR `blocked` label is the park vocabulary that every rule reads (`notLabels: [blocked]` on PR rules, `_prSideBlockedLabel` for issue-carier rules). The fix: post-action sets PR `blocked` + strips arms on both carriers. AC2 first half satisfied. Second half: "moving the issue off status:Blocked" — for that to re-admit, `status:Blocked` must also freeze; but it currently doesn't freeze anything, so moving off it is trivialy "enough" (it never blocked re-admission in the SM). Wait but does the issue-carier freeze apply through the PR? `_prLabelGuardsFail` reads the linked PR's labels for issue-carier rules. So once PR gets `blocked`, issue rules freeze too. Removing PR `blocked` unfreezes. And `status:Blocked` on issue is never read by SM — so it neither blocks nor requires clearing. "Moving the issue off status:Blocked is enough for re-admission" holds trivialy. Hmm, but should status:Blocked ALSO freeze issue rules so that removing PR blocked alone doesn't re-admit while issue still says Blocked? AC2 says either action is enough — meaning we should NOT require both. So: freeze = PR blocked label only (existing engine behavior). If a human removes PR blocked but leaves issue status:Blocked, pair re-admits — and that's per AC2 acceptable ("a human owns the blocked state by design", non-goal auto-unblock). Actually strictly, AC2 says both are sufficient paths; it doesn't say the states must be synced. But for robustness, maybe also strip status:Blocked when PR blocked removed? That's an SM rule change — out of scope, and there's no such rule currently and adding auto-unblock heuristics is a non-goal. Unblocking symmetric: human removing `blocked` from the PR (or moving issue off status:Blocked) re-admits the pair. — Since PR `blocked` label already freezes the issue-carier items in `_prSideBlockedLabel` and PR-side `notLabels: [blocked]` in rules, removing the label re-admits. Hmm — so both directions must re-admit: remove PR blocked label OR remove issue status:Blocked label. If SM rules only freeze on the PR `blocked` label, then removing `blocked` from PR re-admits, but if the issue still has `status:Blocked`... would rules re-admit? For issue-carier rules: they query issues and match labels. Does the issue still carry `agent:rework`? We strip it. Does `status:Blocked` freeze issue rules? Apparently not — "No SM rule reads status:Blocked". Hmm, but that's arguably the desired re-admission per AC2: "moving the issue off status:Blocked is enough for re-admission" — means while status:Blocked remains, should it stay frozen? AC2 second path: "moving the issue off status:Blocked is enough for re-admission". Currently SM never reads `status:Blocked` on the issue — so it neither freezes nor blocks re-admission. If the human removes `blocked` from the PR but the issue still carries `status:Blocked`, the pair re-admits — consistent with "removing blocked from the PR is enough". And moving the issue off status:Blocked — since SM doesn't read it, there's no hidden switch: it's trivialy enough. But hmm — should the issue's `status:Blocked` label ALSO freeze? AC2 says a human removing the PR label OR moving the issue off Blocked re-admits. If both must be cleared, that would violate "either is enough". So no SM change needed for AC2 — the semantics already hold: PR `blocked` is the one park switch, and it's human-removable. The post-action must ensure the issue no longer carries arms (agent:rework/agent:review) so that after a human removes `blocked`, standard lanes re-admit without leftover arms causing immediate rework.

Engine-level: `blocked` on the PR freezes both PR-type items and issue-carier items. So parking the PR with `blocked` fully freezes the pair; removing `blocked` re-admits the pair (AC2 first path).

AC2 second path: "moving the issue off status:Blocked is enough for re-admission". Currently SM never reads `status:Blocked` on the issue — so it neither freezes nor blocks re-admission. If the human removes `blocked` from the PR but the issue still carries `status:Blocked`, the pair re-admits — consistent with "removing blocked from the PR is enough". And moving the issue off status:Blocked — since SM doesn't read it, there's no hidden switch: it's trivialy enough. But hmm — should the issue's `status:Blocked` label ALSO freeze? AC2 says a human removing the PR label OR moving the issue off Blocked re-admits. If both must be cleared, that would violate "either is enough". So no SM change needed for AC2 — the semantics already hold: PR `blocked` is the one park switch, and it's human-removable. The post-action must ensure the issue no longer carries arms (agent:rework/agent:review) so that after a human removes `blocked`, standard lanes re-admit without leftover arms causing immediate rework.

Also AC3: unit test — simulated blocked conclusion → PR carries `blocked`, arms gone, next tick dispatches nothing for the pair. The unit test should test handleReworkBlocked's new behavior plus possibly githubSource guard (already covered by existing test_smGithubSource.js?). Acceptance criteria:
1. When a rework/dev leg concludes BLOCKED, the post-action ALSO labels the linked PR `blocked` and strips `agent:rework`/`agent:review` arms from both the PR and the issue — one atomic park.
2. Unblocking symmetric: human removing `blocked` from the PR (or moving issue off status:Blocked) re-admits the pair. — Since PR `blocked` label already freezes the issue-carier items in `_prSideBlockedLabel` and PR-side `notLabels: [blocked]` in rules, removing the label re-admits. Need to verify issue rules also carry `blocked` in notLabels... In gh mode, issue rules match on issue labels; do they carry notLabels blocked? Let's check what labels freeze issue rules. `_issueCarrierGuardsFail` — check that function. Also, does `status:Blocked` on the issue freeze issue rules? The ticket says "No SM rule reads status:Blocked". AC2 says moving issue off status:Blocked is enough for standard lanes to re-admit the pair — that means issue rules should exclude `status:Blocked` issues too? Actually re-read: "Unblocking is symmetric: a human removing `blocked` from the PR (or moving the issue off `status:Blocked`) is enough for the standard lanes to re-admit the pair (no hidden second switch)." Hmm — so both directions must re-admit: remove PR blocked label OR remove issue status:Blocked label. If SM rules only freeze on the PR `blocked` label, then removing `blocked` from PR re-admits, but if the issue still has `status:Blocked`... would rules re-admit? For issue-carier rules: they query issues and match labels. Does the issue still carry `agent:rework`? We strip it. Does `status:Blocked` freeze issue rules? Apparently not — "No SM rule reads status:Blocked". So an issue with `status:Blocked` but no arms and no PR blocked label — would dev-on-assignment re-derive? gh-944 rule: matches assigned issues with no loop marker labels — yes it would re-dispatch. Hmm, but that's arguably the desired re-admission per AC2: "moving the issue off status:Blocked is enough for re-admission" — means while status:Blocked remains, should it stay frozen? AC2's parenthetical says removing EITHER is enough. That implies while status:Blocked is present but PR blocked was removed... ambiguous. Simplest reading: no hidden second switch — a single action suffices to unblock. The two "blocked" indicators should be equivalent. So ideally: PR blocked label OR issue status:Blocked label both freeze; removing either... if both are set, removing one leaves the other — "enough" implies removing one suffices even if the other remains? That would require SM to treat them as one logical state OR the post-action to set both and... hmm.

Actually the cleanest interpretation given the SM engine: the PR `blocked` label is the park vocabulary that every rule reads (`notLabels: [blocked]` on PR rules, `_prSideBlockedLabel` for issue-carier rules). The fix: post-action sets PR `blocked` + strips arms on both carriers. AC2 first half satisfied. # gh-1060 RCA

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: When a rework leg concludes BLOCKED (agents#827 contract), only the ISSUE gets `status:Blocked`; the linked PR keeps its `agent:rework` arm and every SM tick re-dispatches a rework leg on a ticket the leg itself declared blocked (live: dmtools-dart gh-395 / PR #420, run 39156398849, 2026-10-18 18:55Z).

**Root cause**: Two parallel "blocked" vocabularies with no bridge. The rework post-action `handleReworkBlocked` in `js/pushReworkChanges.js` (~line 1498) calls `tracker.moveToStatus(ticketKey, Blocked)` (→ issue label `status:Blocked` in gh mode) but never touches the PR. The SM's park vocabulary is the PR-side `blocked` label, which IS engine-level (`js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: `matchesGuards` line ~313/476 and `queryPrs` line ~1131 freeze any PR — and issue-carrier items via the linked PR — carrying `blocked`), and every rule's lanes re-admit automatically when a human removes it. No SM rule reads the issue-side `status:Blocked`, so the armed PR loops rework legs until a human strips the label manually.

**Impact**: Any rework leg concluding blocked on a gh-mode deployment leaves the PR armed; each subsequent SM tick dispatches a fresh rework leg (token burn) on a blocked ticket. Human had to intervene manually in the live incident.

**Fix approach**: Bridge the vocabularies at the single writer site — `handleReworkBlocked` performs one atomic park: label the PR `blocked` (scm.addLabel) and strip `agent:rework`/`agent:review` from BOTH the PR (scm.removeLabel) and the issue (tracker.removeLabel). Unblocking needs no new code: the engine already freezes/unfreezes on the PR `blocked` label (removing it re-admits the pair to all standard lanes), and no rule reads `status:Blocked`, so there is no hidden second switch (AC2). No auto-unblock heuristic added (non-goal).

**Dev leg note**: the dev leg's blocked path (`completeBlockedPath` in `js/developBugAndCreatePR.js`) runs after Path 0, which returns early whenever an open PR for the branch exists — at blocked-conclusion time there is no linked PR to park by construction, so the bridge belongs solely in the rework post-action.

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: When a rework leg concludes BLOCKED (agents#827 contract), only the ISSUE gets `status:Blocked`; the linked PR keeps its `agent:rework` arm and every SM tick re-dispatches a rework leg on a ticket the leg itself declared blocked (live: dmtools-dart gh-395 / PR #420, run 39156398849, 2026-10-18 18:55Z).

**Root cause**: Two parallel "blocked" vocabularies with no bridge. The rework post-action `handleReworkBlocked` in `js/pushReworkChanges.js` (~line 1498) calls `tracker.moveToStatus(ticketKey, Blocked)` (→ issue label `status:Blocked` in gh mode) but never touches the PR. The SM's park vocabulary is the PR-side `blocked` label, which IS engine-level (`js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: `matchesGuards` line ~313/476 and `queryPrs` line ~1131 freeze any PR — and issue-carrier items via the linked PR — carrying `blocked`), and every rule's lanes re-admit automatically when a human removes it. No SM rule reads the issue-side `status:Blocked`, so the armed PR loops rework legs until a human strips the label manually.

**Impact**: Any rework leg concluding blocked on a gh-mode deployment leaves the PR armed; each subsequent SM tick dispatches a fresh rework leg (token burn) on a blocked ticket. Human had to intervene manually in the live incident.

**Fix approach**: Bridge the vocabularies at the single writer site — `handleReworkBlocked` performs one atomic park: label the PR `blocked` (scm.addLabel) and strip `agent:rework`/`agent:review` from BOTH the PR (scm.removeLabel) and the issue (tracker.removeLabel). Unblocking needs no new code: the engine already freezes/unfreezes on the PR `blocked` label (removing it re-admits the pair to all standard lanes), and no rule reads `status:Blocked`, so there is no hidden second switch (AC2). No auto-unblock heuristic added (non-goal).

**Dev leg note**: the dev leg's blocked path (`completeBlockedPath` in `js/developBugAndCreatePR.js`) runs after Path 0, which returns early whenever an open PR for the branch exists — at blocked-conclusion time there is no linked PR to park by construction, so the bridge belongs solely in the rework post-action.

{"content":"# gh-1060 RCA

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: When a rework leg concludes BLOCKED (agents#827 contract), only the ISSUE gets `status:Blocked`; the linked PR keeps its `agent:rework` arm and every SM tick re-dispatches a rework leg on a ticket the leg itself declared blocked (live: dmtools-dart gh-395 / PR #420, run 39156398849, 2026-10-18 18:55Z).

**Root cause**: Two parallel "blocked" vocabularies with no bridge. The rework post-action `handleReworkBlocked` in `js/pushReworkChanges.js` (~line 1498) calls `tracker.moveToStatus(ticketKey, Blocked)` (→ issue label `status:Blocked` in gh mode) but never touches the PR. The SM's park vocabulary is the PR-side `blocked` label, which IS engine-level (`js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: `matchesGuards` line ~313/476 and `queryPrs` line ~1131 freeze any PR — and issue-carrier items via the linked PR — carrying `blocked`), and every rule's lanes re-admit automatically when a human removes it. No SM rule reads the issue-side `status:Blocked`, so the armed PR loops rework legs until a human strips the label manually.

**Impact**: Any rework leg concluding blocked on a gh-mode deployment leaves the PR armed; each subsequent SM tick dispatches a fresh rework leg (token burn) on a blocked ticket. Human had to intervene manually in the live incident.

**Fix approach**: Bridge the vocabularies at the single writer site — `handleReworkBlocked` performs one atomic park: label the PR `blocked` (scm.addLabel) and strip `agent:rework`/`agent:review` from BOTH the PR (scm.removeLabel) and the issue (tracker.removeLabel). Unblocking needs no new code: the engine already freezes/unfreezes on the PR `blocked` label (removing it re-admits the pair to all standard lanes), and no rule reads `status:Blocked`, so there is no hidden second switch (AC2). No auto-unblock heuristic added (non-goal).

**Dev leg note**: the dev leg's blocked path (`completeBlockedPath` in `js/developBugAndCreatePR.js`) runs after Path 0, which returns early whenever an open PR for the branch exists — at blocked-conclusion time there is no linked PR to park by construction, so the bridge belongs solely in the rework post-action.

Engine-level: `blocked` on the PR freezes both PR-type items and issue-carier items. So parking the PR with `blocked` fully freezes the pair; removing `blocked` re-admits the pair (AC2 first path).

AC2 second path: "moving the issue off status:Blocked is enough for re-admission". Currently SM never reads `status:Blocked` on the issue — so it neither freezes nor blocks re-admission. If the human removes `blocked` from the PR but the issue still carries `status:Blocked`, the pair re-admits — consistent with "removing blocked from the PR is enough". And moving the issue off status:Blocked — since SM doesn't read it, there's no hidden switch: it's trivialy enough. But hmm — should the issue's `status:Blocked` label ALSO freeze? AC2 says a human removing the PR label OR moving the issue off Blocked re-admits. If both must be cleared, that would violate "either is enough". So no SM change needed for AC2 — the semantics already hold: PR `blocked` is the one park switch, and it's human-removable. The post-action must ensure the issue no longer carries arms (agent:rework/agent:review) so that after a human removes `blocked`, standard lanes re-admit without leftover arms causing immediate rework.

Also AC3: unit test — simulated blocked conclusion → PR carries `blocked`, arms gone, next tick dispatches nothing for the pair. {"content":"# gh-1060 RCA

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: When a rework leg concludes BLOCKED (agents#827 contract), only the ISSUE gets `status:Blocked`; the linked PR keeps its `agent:rework` arm and every SM tick re-dispatches a rework leg on a ticket the leg itself declared blocked (live: dmtools-dart gh-395 / PR #420, run 39156398849, 2026-10-18 18:55Z).

**Root cause**: Two parallel "blocked" vocabularies with no bridge. The rework post-action `handleReworkBlocked` in `js/pushReworkChanges.js` (~line 1498) calls `tracker.moveToStatus(ticketKey, Blocked)` (→ issue label `status:Blocked` in gh mode) but never touches the PR. The SM's park vocabulary is the PR-side `blocked` label, which IS engine-level (`js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: `matchesGuards` line ~313/476 and `queryPrs` line ~1131 freeze any PR — and issue-carrier items via the linked PR — carrying `blocked`), and every rule's lanes re-admit automatically when a human removes it. No SM rule reads the issue-side `status:Blocked`, so the armed PR loops rework legs until a human strips the label manually.

**Impact**: Any rework leg concluding blocked on a gh-mode deployment leaves the PR armed; each subsequent SM tick dispatches a fresh rework leg (token burn) on a blocked ticket. Human had to intervene manually in the live incident.

**Fix approach**: Bridge the vocabularies at the single writer site — `handleReworkBlocked` performs one atomic park: label the PR `blocked` (scm.addLabel) and strip `agent:rework`/`agent:review` from BOTH the PR (scm.removeLabel) and the issue (tracker.removeLabel). Unblocking needs no new code: the engine already freezes/unfreezes on the PR `blocked` label (removing it re-admits the pair to all standard lanes), and no rule reads `status:Blocked`, so there is no hidden second switch (AC2). No auto-unblock heuristic added (non-goal).

**Dev leg note**: the dev leg's blocked path (`completeBlockedPath` in `js/developBugAndCreatePR.js`) runs after Path 0, which returns early whenever an open PR for the branch exists — at blocked-conclusion time there is no linked PR to park by construction, so the bridge belongs solely in the rework post-action.

Acceptance criteria:
1. When a rework/dev leg concludes BLOCKED, the post-action ALSO labels the linked PR `blocked` and strips `agent:rework`/`agent:review` arms from both the PR and the issue — one atomic park.
2. Unblocking symmetric: human removing `blocked` from the PR (or moving issue off status:Blocked) re-admits the pair. — Since PR `blocked` label already freezes the issue-carier items in `_prSideBlockedLabel` and PR-side `notLabels: [blocked]` in rules, removing the label re-admits. Need to verify issue rules also carry `blocked` in notLabels... In gh mode, issue rules match on issue labels; do they carry notLabels blocked? Let's check what labels freeze issue rules. `_issueCarrierGuardsFail` — check that function. Also, does `status:Blocked` on the issue freeze issue rules? The ticket says "No SM rule reads status:Blocked". AC2 says moving issue off status:Blocked is enough for standard lanes to re-admit the pair — that means issue rules should exclude `status:Blocked` issues too? Actually re-read: "Unblocking is symmetric: a human removing `blocked` from the PR (or moving the issue off `status:Blocked`) is enough for the standard lanes to re-admit the pair (no hidden second switch)." Hmm — so both directions must re-admit: remove PR blocked label OR remove issue status:Blocked label. If SM rules only freeze on the PR `blocked` label, then removing `blocked` from PR re-admits, but if the issue still has `status:Blocked`... would rules re-admit? For issue-carier rules: they query issues and match labels. Does the issue still carry `agent:rework`? We strip it. Does `status:Blocked` freeze issue rules? Apparently not — "No SM rule reads status:Blocked". So an issue with `status:Blocked` but no arms and no PR blocked label — would dev-on-assignment re-derive? gh-944 rule: matches assigned issues with no loop marker labels — yes it would re-dispatch. Hmm, but that's arguably the desired re-admission per AC2: "moving the issue off status:Blocked is enough for re-admission" — means while status:Blocked remains, should it stay frozen? AC2's parenthetical says removing EITHER is enough. That implies while status:Blocked is present but PR blocked was removed... ambiguous. Simplest reading: no hidden second switch — a single action suffices to unblock. The two "blocked" indicators should be equivalent. So ideally: PR blocked label OR issue status:Blocked label both freeze; removing either... if both are set, removing one leaves the other — "enough" implies removing one suffices even if the other remains? That would require SM to treat them as one logical state OR the post-action to set both and... hmm.

Actually the cleanest interpretation given the SM engine: the PR `blocked` label is the park vocabulary that every rule reads (`notLabels: [blocked]` on PR rules, `_prSideBlockedLabel` for issue-carier rules). {"content":"# gh-1060 RCA

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: When a rework leg concludes BLOCKED (agents#827 contract), only the ISSUE gets `status:Blocked`; the linked PR keeps its `agent:rework` arm and every SM tick re-dispatches a rework leg on a ticket the leg itself declared blocked (live: dmtools-dart gh-395 / PR #420, run 39156398849, 2026-10-18 18:55Z).

**Root cause**: Two parallel "blocked" vocabularies with no bridge. The rework post-action `handleReworkBlocked` in `js/pushReworkChanges.js` (~line 1498) calls `tracker.moveToStatus(ticketKey, Blocked)` (→ issue label `status:Blocked` in gh mode) but never touches the PR. The SM's park vocabulary is the PR-side `blocked` label, which IS engine-level (`js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: `matchesGuards` line ~313/476 and `queryPrs` line ~1131 freeze any PR — and issue-carrier items via the linked PR — carrying `blocked`), and every rule's lanes re-admit automatically when a human removes it. No SM rule reads the issue-side `status:Blocked`, so the armed PR loops rework legs until a human strips the label manually.

**Impact**: Any rework leg concluding blocked on a gh-mode deployment leaves the PR armed; each subsequent SM tick dispatches a fresh rework leg (token burn) on a blocked ticket. Human had to intervene manually in the live incident.

**Fix approach**: Bridge the vocabularies at the single writer site — `handleReworkBlocked` performs one atomic park: label the PR `blocked` (scm.addLabel) and strip `agent:rework`/`agent:review` from BOTH the PR (scm.removeLabel) and the issue (tracker.removeLabel). Unblocking needs no new code: the engine already freezes/unfreezes on the PR `blocked` label (removing it re-admits the pair to all standard lanes), and no rule reads `status:Blocked`, so there is no hidden second switch (AC2). No auto-unblock heuristic added (non-goal).

**Dev leg note**: the dev leg's blocked path (`completeBlockedPath` in `js/developBugAndCreatePR.js`) runs after Path 0, which returns early whenever an open PR for the branch exists — at blocked-conclusion time there is no linked PR to park by construction, so the bridge belongs solely in the rework post-action.

Engine-level: `blocked` on the PR freezes both PR-type items and issue-carier items. So parking the PR with `blocked` fully freezes the pair; removing `blocked` re-admits the pair (AC2 first path).

AC2 second path: "moving the issue off status:Blocked is enough for re-admission". Currently SM never reads `status:Blocked` on the issue — so it neither freezes nor blocks re-admission. If the human removes `blocked` from the PR but the issue still carries `status:Blocked`, the pair re-admits — consistent with "removing blocked from the PR is enough". And moving the issue off status:Blocked — since SM doesn't read it, there's no hidden switch: it's trivialy enough. But hmm — should the issue's `status:Blocked` label ALSO freeze? AC2 says a human removing the PR label OR moving the issue off Blocked re-admits. If both must be cleared, that would violate "either is enough". So no SM change needed for AC2 — the semantics already hold: PR `blocked` is the one park switch, and it's human-removable. The post-action must ensure the issue no longer carries arms (agent:rework/agent:review) so that after a human removes `blocked`, standard lanes re-admit without leftover arms causing immediate rework.

Also AC3: unit test — simulated blocked conclusion → PR carries `blocked`, arms gone, next tick dispatches nothing for the pair. The unit test should test handleReworkBlocked's new behavior plus possibly githubSource guard (already covered by existing test_smGithubSource.js?). {"content":"# gh-1060 RCA

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: When a rework leg concludes BLOCKED (agents#827 contract), only the ISSUE gets `status:Blocked`; the linked PR keeps its `agent:rework` arm and every SM tick re-dispatches a rework leg on a ticket the leg itself declared blocked (live: dmtools-dart gh-395 / PR #420, run 39156398849, 2026-10-18 18:55Z).

**Root cause**: Two parallel "blocked" vocabularies with no bridge. The rework post-action `handleReworkBlocked` in `js/pushReworkChanges.js` (~line 1498) calls `tracker.moveToStatus(ticketKey, Blocked)` (→ issue label `status:Blocked` in gh mode) but never touches the PR. The SM's park vocabulary is the PR-side `blocked` label, which IS engine-level (`js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: `matchesGuards` line ~313/476 and `queryPrs` line ~1131 freeze any PR — and issue-carrier items via the linked PR — carrying `blocked`), and every rule's lanes re-admit automatically when a human removes it. No SM rule reads the issue-side `status:Blocked`, so the armed PR loops rework legs until a human strips the label manually.

**Impact**: Any rework leg concluding blocked on a gh-mode deployment leaves the PR armed; each subsequent SM tick dispatches a fresh rework leg (token burn) on a blocked ticket. Human had to intervene manually in the live incident.

**Fix approach**: Bridge the vocabularies at the single writer site — `handleReworkBlocked` performs one atomic park: label the PR `blocked` (scm.addLabel) and strip `agent:rework`/`agent:review` from BOTH the PR (scm.removeLabel) and the issue (tracker.removeLabel). Unblocking needs no new code: the engine already freezes/unfreezes on the PR `blocked` label (removing it re-admits the pair to all standard lanes), and no rule reads `status:Blocked`, so there is no hidden second switch (AC2). No auto-unblock heuristic added (non-goal).

**Dev leg note**: the dev leg's blocked path (`completeBlockedPath` in `js/developBugAndCreatePR.js`) runs after Path 0, which returns early whenever an open PR for the branch exists — at blocked-conclusion time there is no linked PR to park by construction, so the bridge belongs solely in the rework post-action.

{"content":"# gh-1060 RCA

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: When a rework leg concludes BLOCKED (agents#827 contract), only the ISSUE gets `status:Blocked`; the linked PR keeps its `agent:rework` arm and every SM tick re-dispatches a rework leg on a ticket the leg itself declared blocked (live: dmtools-dart gh-395 / PR #420, run 39156398849, 2026-10-18 18:55Z).

**Root cause**: Two parallel "blocked" vocabularies with no bridge. The rework post-action `handleReworkBlocked` in `js/pushReworkChanges.js` (~line 1498) calls `tracker.moveToStatus(ticketKey, Blocked)` (→ issue label `status:Blocked` in gh mode) but never touches the PR. The SM's park vocabulary is the PR-side `blocked` label, which IS engine-level (`js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: `matchesGuards` line ~313/476 and `queryPrs` line ~1131 freeze any PR — and issue-carrier items via the linked PR — carrying `blocked`), and every rule's lanes re-admit automatically when a human removes it. No SM rule reads the issue-side `status:Blocked`, so the armed PR loops rework legs until a human strips the label manually.

**Impact**: Any rework leg concluding blocked on a gh-mode deployment leaves the PR armed; each subsequent SM tick dispatches a fresh rework leg (token burn) on a blocked ticket. Human had to intervene manually in the live incident.

**Fix approach**: Bridge the vocabularies at the single writer site — `handleReworkBlocked` performs one atomic park: label the PR `blocked` (scm.addLabel) and strip `agent:rework`/`agent:review` from BOTH the PR (scm.removeLabel) and the issue (tracker.removeLabel). Unblocking needs no new code: the engine already freezes/unfreezes on the PR `blocked` label (removing it re-admits the pair to all standard lanes), and no rule reads `status:Blocked`, so there is no hidden second switch (AC2). No auto-unblock heuristic added (non-goal).

**Dev leg note**: the dev leg's blocked path (`completeBlockedPath` in `js/developBugAndCreatePR.js`) runs after Path 0, which returns early whenever an open PR for the branch exists — at blocked-conclusion time there is no linked PR to park by construction, so the bridge belongs solely in the rework post-action.

Engine-level: `blocked` on the PR freezes both PR-type items and issue-carier items. So parking the PR with `blocked` fully freezes the pair; removing `blocked` re-admits the pair (AC2 first path).

AC2 second path: "moving the issue off status:Blocked is enough for re-admission". Currently SM never reads `status:Blocked` on the issue — so it neither freezes nor blocks re-admission. If the human removes `blocked` from the PR but the issue still carries `status:Blocked`, the pair re-admits — consistent with "removing blocked from the PR is enough". And moving the issue off status:Blocked — since SM doesn't read it, there's no hidden switch: it's trivialy enough. But hmm — should the issue's `status:Blocked` label ALSO freeze? AC2 says a human removing the PR label OR moving the issue off Blocked re-admits. If both must be cleared, that would violate "either is enough". So no SM change needed for AC2 — the semantics already hold: PR `blocked` is the one park switch, and it's human-removable. The post-action must ensure the issue no longer carries arms (agent:rework/agent:review) so that after a human removes `blocked`, standard lanes re-admit without leftover arms causing immediate rework.

Also AC3: unit test — simulated blocked conclusion → PR carries `blocked`, arms gone, next tick dispatches nothing for the pair. {"content":"# gh-1060 RCA

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: When a rework leg concludes BLOCKED (agents#827 contract), only the ISSUE gets `status:Blocked`; the linked PR keeps its `agent:rework` arm and every SM tick re-dispatches a rework leg on a ticket the leg itself declared blocked (live: dmtools-dart gh-395 / PR #420, run 39156398849, 2026-10-18 18:55Z).

**Root cause**: Two parallel "blocked" vocabularies with no bridge. The rework post-action `handleReworkBlocked` in `js/pushReworkChanges.js` (~line 1498) calls `tracker.moveToStatus(ticketKey, Blocked)` (→ issue label `status:Blocked` in gh mode) but never touches the PR. The SM's park vocabulary is the PR-side `blocked` label, which IS engine-level (`js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: `matchesGuards` line ~313/476 and `queryPrs` line ~1131 freeze any PR — and issue-carrier items via the linked PR — carrying `blocked`), and every rule's lanes re-admit automatically when a human removes it. No SM rule reads the issue-side `status:Blocked`, so the armed PR loops rework legs until a human strips the label manually.

**Impact**: Any rework leg concluding blocked on a gh-mode deployment leaves the PR armed; each subsequent SM tick dispatches a fresh rework leg (token burn) on a blocked ticket. Human had to intervene manually in the live incident.

**Fix approach**: Bridge the vocabularies at the single writer site — `handleReworkBlocked` performs one atomic park: label the PR `blocked` (scm.addLabel) and strip `agent:rework`/`agent:review` from BOTH the PR (scm.removeLabel) and the issue (tracker.removeLabel). Unblocking needs no new code: the engine already freezes/unfreezes on the PR `blocked` label (removing it re-admits the pair to all standard lanes), and no rule reads `status:Blocked`, so there is no hidden second switch (AC2). No auto-unblock heuristic added (non-goal).

**Dev leg note**: the dev leg's blocked path (`completeBlockedPath` in `js/developBugAndCreatePR.js`) runs after Path 0, which returns early whenever an open PR for the branch exists — at blocked-conclusion time there is no linked PR to park by construction, so the bridge belongs solely in the rework post-action.

{"content":"# gh-1060 RCA

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: When a rework leg concludes BLOCKED (agents#827 contract), only the ISSUE gets `status:Blocked`; the linked PR keeps its `agent:rework` arm and every SM tick re-dispatches a rework leg on a ticket the leg itself declared blocked (live: dmtools-dart gh-395 / PR #420, run 39156398849, 2026-10-18 18:55Z).

**Root cause**: Two parallel "blocked" vocabularies with no bridge. The rework post-action `handleReworkBlocked` in `js/pushReworkChanges.js` (~line 1498) calls `tracker.moveToStatus(ticketKey, Blocked)` (→ issue label `status:Blocked` in gh mode) but never touches the PR. The SM's park vocabulary is the PR-side `blocked` label, which IS engine-level (`js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: `matchesGuards` line ~313/476 and `queryPrs` line ~1131 freeze any PR — and issue-carrier items via the linked PR — carrying `blocked`), and every rule's lanes re-admit automatically when a human removes it. No SM rule reads the issue-side `status:Blocked`, so the armed PR loops rework legs until a human strips the label manually.

**Impact**: Any rework leg concluding blocked on a gh-mode deployment leaves the PR armed; each subsequent SM tick dispatches a fresh rework leg (token burn) on a blocked ticket. Human had to intervene manually in the live incident.

**Fix approach**: Bridge the vocabularies at the single writer site — `handleReworkBlocked` performs one atomic park: label the PR `blocked` (scm.addLabel) and strip `agent:rework`/`agent:review` from BOTH the PR (scm.removeLabel) and the issue (tracker.removeLabel). Unblocking needs no new code: the engine already freezes/unfreezes on the PR `blocked` label (removing it re-admits the pair to all standard lanes), and no rule reads `status:Blocked`, so there is no hidden second switch (AC2). No auto-unblock heuristic added (non-goal).

**Dev leg note**: the dev leg's blocked path (`completeBlockedPath` in `js/developBugAndCreatePR.js`) runs after Path 0, which returns early whenever an open PR for the branch exists — at blocked-conclusion time there is no linked PR to park by construction, so the bridge belongs solely in the rework post-action.
